title.en: Genealogical Tables of the Three Dynasties

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：五帝、三代之記，尚矣。

translations.literal: Grand Historian says: Five Emperors, Three Dynasties records, remote.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: The records of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties go back to great antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自殷以前諸侯不可得而譜，周以來乃頗可著。

translations.literal: From Yin before feudal lords cannot be obtained to arrange genealogy, Zhou since then considerably can be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Yin dynasty, the genealogies of the feudal lords cannot be fixed; only from the Zhou dynasty onward can they be recorded with confidence.

sentences.zh: 孔子因史文次春秋，紀元年，正時日月，蓋其詳哉。

translations.literal: Confucius followed historical texts arranged Spring and Autumn, recorded first year, corrected seasons days months, indeed detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius followed the historical texts to arrange the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording the first year and correcting the seasons, days, and months—how detailed it is!

sentences.zh: 至於序尚書則略，無年月；

translations.literal: As for arranging Shangshu then brief, without years months;
translations.idiomatic: As for arranging the Shangshu, it is brief, without years or months;

sentences.zh: 或頗有，然多闕，不可錄。

translations.literal: Some considerably have, yet many deficient, cannot record.
translations.idiomatic: Some have quite a bit, but many are deficient and cannot be recorded.

sentences.zh: 故疑則傳疑，蓋其慎也。

translations.literal: Therefore, doubt then transmit doubt, indeed cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, where there is doubt, transmit the doubt—that is how cautious he was.

sentences.zh: 余讀諜記，黃帝以來皆有年數。

translations.literal: I read the genealogical records; from the Yellow Emperor onward all have year counts.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the genealogical records, and from the Yellow Emperor onward they all have chronological dates.

sentences.zh: 稽其歷譜諜終始五德之傳，古文咸不同，乖異。

translations.literal: Examining their chronological genealogies and registers, and the transmission of the Five Virtues from beginning to end, the ancient texts are all different and at odds.
translations.idiomatic: When I examined their chronological genealogies and the transmission of the Five Virtues from beginning to end, the ancient texts are all different and contradictory.

sentences.zh: 夫子之弗論次其年月，豈虛哉！

translations.literal: That the Master did not arrange their years and months—was that without good reason!
translations.idiomatic: That the Master did not arrange their years and months—was that not well-founded!

sentences.zh: 於是以五帝繫諜、尚書集世紀黃帝以來訖共和爲世表。

translations.literal: Thereupon I used the Five Emperors genealogical records and the collected chronicles of the Shangshu to compile a genealogical table from the Yellow Emperor down to the Gonghe era.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon I used the Five Emperors' genealogical records and the collected chronicles of the Shangshu to compile a genealogical table from the Yellow Emperor down to the Gonghe era.

sentences.zh: 帝王世國號

translations.literal: Imperial age and state title
translations.idiomatic: Imperial reigns and state designations

sentences.zh: 顓頊屬

translations.literal: Zhuanxu line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Zhuanxu

sentences.zh: 俈屬

translations.literal: Ku line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Ku

sentences.zh: 堯屬

translations.literal: Yao line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Yao

sentences.zh: 舜屬

translations.literal: Shun line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Shun

sentences.zh: 夏屬

translations.literal: Xia line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Xia

sentences.zh: 殷屬

translations.literal: Yin line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Yin

sentences.zh: 周屬

translations.literal: Zhou line
translations.idiomatic: Line of Zhou

cells.literal: The Yellow Emperor, styled Lord of Youxiong.
cells.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor, with the style Lord of Youxiong.

cells.content: 帝顓頊，黃帝孫。起黃帝，至顓頊三世，號高陽。
cells.literal: Emperor Zhuanxu, grandson of the Yellow Emperor. From the Yellow Emperor to Zhuanxu, three generations, styled Gaoyang.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanxu, the Yellow Emperor's grandson. From the Yellow Emperor to Zhuanxu: three generations, with the style Gaoyang.

cells.literal: Changyi begot Zhuanxu, who became the Gaoyang clan.
cells.idiomatic: Changyi fathered Zhuanxu, who took the Gaoyang clan name.

cells.content: 昌意生顓頊。顓頊生窮蟬。
cells.literal: Changyi begot Zhuanxu. Zhuanxu begot Qiongchan.
cells.idiomatic: Changyi fathered Zhuanxu. Zhuanxu fathered Qiongchan.

cells.content: 玄囂生蟜極。蟜極生高辛。
cells.literal: Xuanxiao begot Jiaoji. Jiaoji begot Gaoxin.
cells.idiomatic: Xuanxiao fathered Jiaoji. Jiaoji fathered Gaoxin.

cells.content: 玄囂生蟜極。蟜極生高辛。
cells.literal: Xuanxiao begot Jiaoji. Jiaoji begot Gaoxin.
cells.idiomatic: Xuanxiao fathered Jiaoji. Jiaoji fathered Gaoxin.

cells.content: 帝俈，黃帝曾孫。起黃帝，至帝俈四世。號高辛。
cells.literal: Emperor Ku, great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor. From the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Ku, four generations. Styled Gaoxin.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Ku, the Yellow Emperor's great-grandson. From the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Ku: four generations, with the style Gaoxin.

cells.literal: Jiaoji begot Gaoxin, who became Emperor Ku.
cells.idiomatic: Jiaoji fathered Gaoxin, who became Emperor Ku.

cells.content: 蟜極生高辛。高辛生放勛。
cells.literal: Jiaoji begot Gaoxin. Gaoxin begot Fangxun.
cells.idiomatic: Jiaoji fathered Gaoxin. Gaoxin fathered Fangxun.

cells.content: 窮蟬生敬康。敬康生句望。
cells.literal: Qiongchan begot Jingkang. Jingkang begot Gouwang.
cells.idiomatic: Qiongchan fathered Jingkang. Jingkang fathered Gouwang.

cells.literal: Gaoxin begot Xie, ancestor of Yin.
cells.idiomatic: Gaoxin fathered Xie, the ancestor of the Yin line.

cells.literal: Gaoxin begot Hou Ji, ancestor of Zhou.
cells.idiomatic: Gaoxin fathered Hou Ji, the ancestor of the Zhou line.

cells.content: 帝堯。起黃帝，至俈子五世。號唐。
cells.literal: Emperor Yao. From the Yellow Emperor to the sons of Ku, five generations. Styled Tang.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Yao. From the Yellow Emperor to the sons of Ku: five generations, with the style Tang.

cells.content: 句望生蟜牛。蟜牛生瞽叟。
cells.literal: Gouwang begot Jiaoniu. Jiaoniu begot Gusou.
cells.idiomatic: Gouwang fathered Jiaoniu. Jiaoniu fathered Gusou.

cells.content: 帝舜，黃帝玄孫之玄孫，號虞。
cells.literal: Emperor Shun, the Yellow Emperor's great-great-grandson's great-great-grandson, styled Yu.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Shun, a great-great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor's great-great-grandson, with the style Yu.

cells.literal: Gusou begot Chonghua; this was Emperor Shun.
cells.idiomatic: Gusou fathered Chonghua, who was Emperor Shun.

cells.literal: Zhuanxu begot Gun. Gun begot Wenming.
cells.idiomatic: Zhuanxu fathered Gun. Gun fathered Wenming.

cells.literal: Emperor Yu, remote descendant of the Yellow Emperor, styled Xia.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Yu, a remote descendant of the Yellow Emperor, with the style Xia.

cells.literal: Emperor Qi attacked Youhu and composed the Ganshi.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Qi attacked Youhu and composed the Ganshi oath

cells.literal: Emperor Zhongkang, younger brother of Taikang.
Zhu Gui begot Tianyi; this was Tang of Yin.
cells.idiomatic: Zhu Gui fathered Tianyi, who was Tang of Yin.

cells.literal: Emperor Jiong, younger brother of Bujiang.
Ji Li begot King Wen Chang. He improved the hexagrams.
cells.idiomatic: Ji Li fathered King Wen Chang, who improved the hexagrams.

cells.literal: King Wen Chang begot King Wu Fa.
cells.idiomatic: King Wen Chang fathered King Wu Fa.

cells.content: 帝孔甲，不降子。好鬼神，淫亂不好德，二龍去。
cells.literal: Emperor Kongjia, son of Bujiang. He favored spirits and ghosts, was dissolute and did not cherish virtue, and the two dragons departed.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Kongjia, son of Bujiang, favored spirits and ghosts, was dissolute and did not cherish virtue, and the two dragons left.

translations.literal: From Yu to Jie, seventeen generations; from the Yellow Emperor to Jie, twenty generations.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen generations from Yu to Jie; twenty generations from the Yellow Emperor to Jie.

sentences.zh: 從禹至桀十七世，從黃帝至桀二十世。

translations.literal: Tang of Yin replaced the house of Xia; from the Yellow Emperor to Tang, seventeen generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang of Yin replaced the Xia, it was seventeen generations from the Yellow Emperor to Tang.

sentences.zh: 殷湯代夏氏，從黃帝至湯十七世。

cells.content: 帝外丙，湯太子。太丁蚤卒，故立次弟外丙。
cells.literal: Emperor Waibing, heir of Tang. Prince Taiding died young, so the next younger brother Waibing was enthroned.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Waibing, Tang's heir. Prince Taiding died young, so the next younger brother Waibing was installed.

cells.literal: Emperor Zhongren, younger brother of Waibing.

cells.content: 帝太甲，故太子太丁子。淫，伊尹放之桐宮。三年，悔過自責，伊尹乃迎之復位。
cells.literal: Emperor Taijia, son of the former heir Taiding. He was dissolute; Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace. After three years he repented and blamed himself, and Yi Yin welcomed him back to the throne.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Taijia, son of the former heir Taiding, was dissolute. Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace; after three years of repentance Yi Yin restored him.

cells.literal: Emperor Taigeng, younger brother of Woding.

cells.content: 帝小甲，太庚弟。殷道衰，諸侯或不至。
cells.literal: Emperor Xiaojia, younger brother of Taigeng. The way of Yin declined, and some feudal lords did not come.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojia, Taigeng's younger brother. The way of Yin declined, and some feudal lords failed to attend court.

cells.literal: Emperor Yongji, younger brother of Xiaojia.

cells.content: 帝太戊，雍己弟。以桑穀生，稱中宗。
cells.literal: Emperor Taiwu, younger brother of Yongji. Because mulberry and grain grew together, he was called Zhongzong.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, Yongji's younger brother, was called Zhongzong because mulberry and grain grew together.

cells.literal: Emperor Wairen, younger brother of Zhongding.
Emperor He Danjia, younger brother of Wairen.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor He Danjia, Wairen's younger brother.

cells.literal: Emperor Wojia, younger brother of Zuxin.
Emperor Pangeng, younger brother of Yangjia. He moved the capital to Henan.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Pangeng, Yangjia's younger brother, moved the capital to Henan.

cells.literal: Emperor Xiaoxin, younger brother of Pangeng.
Emperor Xiaoyi, younger brother of Xiaoxin.

cells.content: 帝武丁。雉升鼎耳雊。得傅說。稱高宗。
cells.literal: Emperor Wuding. A pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed. He obtained Fuyue. He was called Gaozong.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Wuding. A pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed; he obtained Fuyue and was called Gaozong.

cells.literal: Emperor Jia, younger brother of Zugeng. He was dissolute.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Jia, Zugeng's younger brother, was dissolute.

cells.content: 帝庚丁，廩辛弟。殷徙河北。
cells.literal: Emperor Gengding, younger brother of Lin Xin. Yin moved north of the River.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Gengding, Lin Xin's younger brother, moved Yin north of the River.

cells.literal: Emperor Wuyi. He slighted the spirits and was killed by thunder.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Wuyi slighted the spirits and was killed by thunder

cells.literal: Emperor Xin; this was Zhou. He was assassinated.
cells.idiomatic: Emperor Xin was Zhou. He was assassinated.

translations.literal: From Tang to Zhou, twenty-nine generations; from the Yellow Emperor to Zhou, forty-six generations.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine generations from Tang to Zhou; forty-six generations from the Yellow Emperor to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 從湯至紂二十九世，從黃帝至紂四十六世。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou replaced Yin; from the Yellow Emperor to King Wu, nineteen generations.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou replaced Yin, it was nineteen generations from the Yellow Emperor to King Wu.

sentences.zh: 周武王代殷，從黃帝至武王十九世。

cells.literal: Lu Zhou Gong Dan, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Lu: Zhou Gong Dan, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.content: 齊太公尚，文王、武王師。初封。
cells.literal: Qi Tai Gong Shang, Wen Wang, Wu Wang teacher. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Qi: Tai Gong Shang, teacher of King Wen and King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Jin Tang Shu Yu, Wu Wang son. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Jin: Tang Shu Yu, son of King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.content: 秦惡來，助紂。父飛廉，有力。
cells.literal: Qin E Lai, assisted Zhou. Father Fei Lian, had strength.
cells.idiomatic: Qin: E Lai, assisted King Zhou. Father Fei Lian, who was strong.

cells.content: 楚熊繹。繹父鬻熊，事文王。初封。
cells.literal: Chu: Xiong Yi. Yi's father Yu Xiong served King Wen. First enfeoffment.
cells.idiomatic: Chu: Xiong Yi. Yi's father Yu Xiong, who served King Wen. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Song Wei Zi Qi, Zhou elder brother by concubine. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Song: Wei Zi Qi, elder brother of King Zhou by a concubine. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Wei Kang Shu, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Wei: Kang Shu, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Chen Hu Gong Man, Shun's descendant. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Chen: Hu Gong Man, descendant of Shun. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Cai Shu Du, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Cai: Shu Du, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Cao Shu Zhen Duo, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Cao: Shu Zhen Duo, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: Yan Zhao Gong Shi, Zhou same surname. First enfeoffed.
cells.idiomatic: Yan: Zhao Gong Shi, of the same surname as Zhou. First enfeoffment.

cells.literal: King Kang (Zhao); punishments were laid aside for more than forty years.
cells.idiomatic: King Kang (Zhao): for more than forty years punishments were laid aside.
Wei Zhong, younger brother of Qi.

cells.content: 昭王瑕南巡不返。不赴，諱之。
cells.literal: King Zhao Xia toured south and did not return. [The lords] did not report it; [the court] concealed it.
cells.idiomatic: King Zhao (Xia) toured the south and did not return. The feudal lords did not report it; the court concealed the matter.

cells.content: 穆王滿。作甫刑。荒服不至。
cells.literal: King Mu Man. Made Fu punishments. Remote regions did not come.
cells.idiomatic: King Mu Man. Made the Punishments of Fu. The remote regions did not come.

cells.literal: Duke Yang, Duke Kao younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: Duke Yang, younger brother of Duke Kao.

cells.literal: Duke Min, Duke Ding younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: Duke Min, younger brother of Duke Ding.

cells.content: 懿王堅。周道衰，詩人作刺。
cells.literal: King Yi Jian. Zhou way declined, poets made satirical poems.
cells.idiomatic: King Yi Jian. The Zhou way declined, poets made satirical poems.

cells.literal: Duke Yang, Duke Min younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: Duke Yang, younger brother of Duke Min.

cells.literal: King Xiao Fang, King Yi younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: King Xiao Fang, younger brother of King Yi.

cells.literal: King Yi Xie, son of King Yi Jian.
cells.idiomatic: King Yi (Xie), son of King Yi (Jian).

cells.literal: Duke Xian, Duke Li younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: Duke Xian, younger brother of Duke Li.

cells.content: 厲王胡。以惡聞過亂，出奔，遂死於彘。
cells.literal: King Li Hu. Because hated hearing criticism caused disorder, fled, then died at Zhi.
cells.idiomatic: King Li Hu. Because he hated hearing the criticism and caused disorder, he fled and died at Zhi.
Xiong Yan, younger brother of Hong.
Gonghe, the two nobles administered government.

cells.literal: Duke Wu, Duke Zhen younger brother.
cells.idiomatic: Duke Wu, younger brother of Duke Zhen.

sentences.zh: 張夫子問褚先生曰：「詩言契、后稷皆無父而生。

translations.literal: Master Zhang asked Master Chu, saying, "The Poetry says Qi and Hou Ji were both born without fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zhang asked Master Chu, saying, "The Poetry says that Qi and Hou Ji were both born without fathers.

sentences.zh: 今案諸傳記咸言有父，父皆黃帝子也，得無與詩謬秋？」

translations.literal: Now examining the various biographies, all say they had fathers; the fathers were all sons of the Yellow Emperor. Could this contradict the Poetry?"
translations.idiomatic: Now when I examine the various biographies they all say they had fathers, and their fathers were all sons of the Yellow Emperor. Could this be at odds with the Poetry?"

sentences.zh: 褚先生曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Master Chu said, "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Master Chu replied, "No, that is not so.

sentences.zh: 詩言契生於卵，后稷人跡者，欲見其有天命精誠之意耳。

translations.literal: Poetry says Qi born from egg, Hou Ji human footprints, wished show had heaven mandate sincere intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry says that Qi was born from an egg, and Hou Ji from human footprints, to show that they had the mandate of heaven and sincere intentions.

sentences.zh: 鬼神不能自成，須人而生，柰何無父而生乎！

translations.literal: Spirits and gods cannot form themselves; they must be born through humans. How could they be born without fathers?
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and gods cannot come into being by themselves; they must be born through human beings. How, then, could they be born without fathers?

sentences.zh: 一言有父，一言無父，信以傳信，疑以傳疑，故兩言之。

translations.literal: One account says they had fathers, and one account says they had no fathers. Transmit what is trustworthy as trustworthy and what is doubtful as doubtful; therefore both accounts are given.
translations.idiomatic: One tradition says they had fathers, while another says they had none. What is trustworthy is transmitted as trustworthy, and what is doubtful as doubtful; for this reason both accounts are recorded.

sentences.zh: 堯知契、稷皆賢人，天之所生，故封之契七十里，後十餘世至湯，王天下。

translations.literal: Yao knew that Qi and Ji were both worthy men, born of Heaven; therefore he enfeoffed Qi with seventy li. After more than ten generations they reached Tang, who ruled all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yao knew that Qi and Ji were both worthy men born of Heaven, and therefore enfeoffed Qi with a domain of seventy li. More than ten generations later, his line reached Tang, who ruled all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 堯知后稷子孫之後王也，故益封之百里，其後世且千歲，至文王而有天下。

translations.literal: Yao knew that Hou Ji's descendants would later become kings; therefore he added a hundred li to his fief. His descendants lasted nearly a thousand years, until King Wen obtained all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yao knew that Hou Ji's descendants would later become kings, and therefore enlarged his fief by a hundred li. His descendants endured for nearly a thousand years, down to King Wen, who came to possess all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 詩傳曰：『湯之先為契，無父而生。

translations.literal: Poetry commentary says, 'Tang's ancestor was Qi, without father born.
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry Commentary says, 'Tang's ancestor was Qi, born without a father.

sentences.zh: 契母與姊妹浴於玄丘水，有燕銜卵墮之，契母得，故含之，誤吞之，即生契。

translations.literal: Qi mother with sisters bathed Xuanhou water, swallow carried egg dropped it, Qi mother obtained, therefore held in mouth, mistakenly swallowed, then gave birth Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's mother and her sisters were bathing in the Xuanhou River, when a swallow carried an egg and dropped it. Qi's mother obtained it, so she held it in her mouth, mistakenly swallowed it, and then gave birth to Qi.

sentences.zh: 契生而賢，堯立為司徒，姓之曰子氏。

translations.literal: Qi born wise, Yao established as Minister of the Multitudes (Situ), surnamed him Zi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was born wise, Yao established him as Minister of the Multitudes (Situ), and gave him the surname Zi.

sentences.zh: 子者茲；

translations.literal: Zi means 'to increase';
translations.idiomatic: Zi means 'to increase';

sentences.zh: 茲，益大也。

translations.literal: This' means to increase and grow great.
translations.idiomatic: To increase means to grow ever greater.

sentences.zh: 詩人美而頌之曰「殷社芒芒，天命玄鳥，降而生商」。

translations.literal: The poets praised and celebrated it, saying, "The Yin altar was vast; Heaven commanded the dark bird to descend and give birth to Shang."
translations.idiomatic: The poets praised and celebrated this, saying, "Vast was the altar of Yin; Heaven commanded the dark bird to descend and give birth to Shang."

sentences.zh: 商者質，殷號也。

translations.literal: Shang means solid, Yin designation.
translations.idiomatic: Shang means solid, it is the designation of Yin.

sentences.zh: 文王之先為后稷，后稷亦無父而生。

translations.literal: Wen Wang's ancestor was Hou Ji, Hou Ji also without father born.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Wang's ancestor was Hou Ji, Hou Ji was also born without a father.

sentences.zh: 后稷母為姜嫄，出見大人蹟而履踐之，知於身，則生后稷。

translations.literal: Hou Ji's mother was Jiang Yuan. She went out, saw a giant footprint, and stepped on it. She felt it in her body and then gave birth to Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji's mother was Jiang Yuan. When she went out, she saw a giant footprint and stepped in it. She felt a response in her body, and then gave birth to Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 姜嫄以為無父，賤而棄之道中，牛羊避不踐也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan thought no father, despised abandoned in road, oxen sheep avoided not tread.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan thought he had no father, so she despised him and abandoned him in the road. Oxen and sheep avoided him and did not tread on him.

sentences.zh: 抱之山中，山者養之。

translations.literal: She carried him into the mountains; mountain folk raised him.
translations.idiomatic: She carried him into the mountains, and the mountain folk raised him.

sentences.zh: 又捐之大澤，鳥覆席食之。

translations.literal: Again cast him great marsh, birds covered wings fed him.
translations.idiomatic: Again she cast him into the great marsh, birds covered him with their wings and fed him.

sentences.zh: 姜嫄怪之，於是知其天子，乃取長之。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan was amazed by this, so she knew he was a child of Heaven and took him back to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan marveled at this, and so knew that he was a child of Heaven; she took him back and raised him.

sentences.zh: 堯知其賢才，立以為大農，姓之曰姬氏。

translations.literal: Yao knew his worthy talents, established as Great Farmer, surnamed him Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao knew his worthy talents, established him as Great Farmer, and gave him the surname Ji.

sentences.zh: 姬者，本也。

translations.literal: Ji means root.
translations.idiomatic: Ji means the root.

sentences.zh: 詩人美而頌之曰「厥初生民」，深修益成，而道后稷之始也。』

translations.literal: The poets praised and celebrated him, saying, "In the beginning he gave birth to the people," deeply cultivating and completing the account of Hou Ji's origins.'
translations.idiomatic: The poets praised and celebrated him, saying, "At the beginning, he gave birth to the people," elaborating and completing the account of Hou Ji's origins.'

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『昔者堯命契為子氏，為有湯也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'Former times Yao commanded Qi to be Zi clan, because would have Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'In former times Yao commanded Qi to be of the Zi clan, because there would be Tang.

sentences.zh: 命后稷為姬氏，為有文王也。

translations.literal: Commanded Hou Ji to be Ji clan, because would have Wen Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Commanded Hou Ji to be of the Ji clan, because there would be Wen Wang.

sentences.zh: 大王命季歷，明天瑞也。

translations.literal: Great King commanded Ji Li, illuminate heavenly omens.
translations.idiomatic: Great King commanded Ji Li, to illuminate the heavenly omens.

sentences.zh: 太伯之吳，遂生源也。』

translations.literal: Tai Bo went Wu, then originated source.'
translations.idiomatic: Tai Bo went to Wu, and thus originated the source.'

sentences.zh: 天命難言，非聖人莫能見。

translations.literal: Heavenly mandate difficult speak, only sages can see.
translations.idiomatic: The heavenly mandate is difficult to speak of, only sages can see it.

sentences.zh: 舜、禹、契、后稷皆黃帝子孫也。

translations.literal: Shun, Yu, Qi, Hou Ji all Yellow Emperor descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Shun, Yu, Qi, and Hou Ji were all descendants of the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 黃帝策天命而治天下，德澤深後世，故其子孫皆復立為天子，是天之報有德也。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor grasped heavenly mandate governed world, virtue grace deep benefited later generations, therefore descendants all again established as sons of heaven, this heaven's reward for virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor grasped the heavenly mandate, governed the world, and left virtue and grace that deeply benefited later generations; therefore his descendants all again became established as sons of heaven—this is heaven's reward for virtue.

sentences.zh: 人不知，以為閒從布衣匹夫起耳。

translations.literal: People not know, think by chance from commoners ordinary men arose.
translations.idiomatic: People do not know this, and think they arose from commoners and ordinary men by chance.

sentences.zh: 夫布衣匹夫安能無故而起王天下乎？

translations.literal: Commoners ordinary men how could without cause arise king world?
translations.idiomatic: How could commoners and ordinary men arise without cause to become kings of the world?

sentences.zh: 其有天命然。」

translations.literal: They had heavenly mandate thus."
translations.idiomatic: It is because they had the heavenly mandate."

sentences.zh: 「黃帝後世何王天下之久遠邪？」

translations.literal: "Yellow Emperor descendants why king world so long?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why did the Yellow Emperor's descendants rule the world so long?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「傳云天下之君王為萬夫之黔首請贖民之命者帝，有福萬世。

translations.literal: He said: "The traditions say that the ruler of the world who pleads to redeem the lives of the common people on behalf of the masses becomes emperor and has good fortune for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The traditions say that the ruler of the world who, on behalf of the multitude, pleads to redeem the lives of the common people becomes an emperor and has good fortune for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 黃帝是也。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor was such.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor was such a one.

sentences.zh: 五政明則修禮義，因天時舉兵征伐而利者王，有福千世。

translations.literal: When the five forms of government are clear, one cultivates ritual and righteousness; those who raise troops for campaigns according to Heaven's timing and gain advantage become kings and have good fortune for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: When the five forms of government are clear, one cultivates ritual and righteousness. Those who raise armies for campaigns in accord with Heaven's timing and thereby gain advantage become kings and have good fortune for a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 蜀王，黃帝後世也，至今在漢西南五千里，常來朝降，輸獻於漢，非以其先之有德，澤流後世邪？

translations.literal: The King of Shu was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor. Even now, five thousand li southwest of Han, he regularly comes to court, submits, and offers tribute to Han. Is this not because his ancestors had virtue and their grace flowed to later generations?
translations.idiomatic: The King of Shu was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor. Even now, though he is five thousand li southwest of Han, he regularly comes to court, submits, and presents tribute to Han. Is this not because his ancestor possessed virtue and his grace flowed down to later generations?

sentences.zh: 行道德豈可以忽乎哉！

translations.literal: To practice morality and virtue—how can one lightly neglect it!
translations.idiomatic: To practice morality and virtue—how can one neglect it!

sentences.zh: 人君王者舉而觀之。

translations.literal: Rulers and kings should take this up and examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers and kings should take up this matter and examine it.

sentences.zh: 漢大將軍霍子孟名光者，亦黃帝後世也。

translations.literal: The Han General-in-Chief Huo Zimeng, named Guang, was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Zimeng, the Han General-in-Chief whose given name was Guang, was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 此可為博聞遠見者言，固難為淺聞者說也。

translations.literal: This can be spoken of to those with broad learning and far sight, but it is certainly difficult to explain to those of shallow knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: This can be discussed with people of broad learning and far sight, but it is certainly difficult to explain to those whose knowledge is shallow.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

sentences.zh: 古諸侯以國為姓。

translations.literal: Ancient feudal lords took state as surname.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the feudal lords took their state as surname.

sentences.zh: 霍者，國名也。

translations.literal: Huo, state name.
translations.idiomatic: Huo was a state name.

sentences.zh: 武王封弟叔處於霍，後世晉獻公滅霍公，後世為庶民，往來居平陽。

translations.literal: King Wu enfeoffed his younger brother Shuchu at Huo. In a later generation, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Huo; his descendants became commoners and moved back and forth, living at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed his younger brother Shuchu at Huo. In a later generation, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Huo, and his descendants became commoners, moving back and forth until they settled at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 平陽在河東，河東晉地，分為衛國。

translations.literal: Pingyang is in Hedong. Hedong was Jin territory and was later divided to become part of the state of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang lies in Hedong. Hedong was Jin territory, and was later partitioned into the state of Wei.

sentences.zh: 以詩言之，亦可為周世。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of the Poetry, this too can be treated as part of the Zhou lineage.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks in terms of the Poetry, this too may be regarded as belonging to the Zhou lineage.

sentences.zh: 周起后稷，后稷無父而生。

translations.literal: Zhou arose from Hou Ji, Hou Ji without father born.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou arose from Hou Ji, Hou Ji was born without a father.

sentences.zh: 以三代世傳言之，后稷有父名高辛；

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Gaoxin;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Gaoxin;

sentences.zh: 高辛，黃帝曾孫。

translations.literal: Gaoxin was the Yellow Emperor's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxin was the great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 黃帝終始傳曰：『漢興百有餘年，有人不短不長，出（自）［白］燕之鄉，持天下之政，時有嬰兒主，欲行車。』

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's Chronicles of Beginning and End say: "More than a hundred years after the Han arose, there will be a man neither short nor tall, coming from the region of Baiyan, holding the government of all under Heaven, at a time when there is an infant ruler who wishes to ride in a carriage."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's Chronicles of Beginning and End says, "More than a hundred years after the Han arises, there will be a man neither short nor tall, from the region of Baiyan, who holds the government of all under Heaven at a time when there is an infant ruler who wishes to ride in a carriage."

sentences.zh: 霍將軍者，本居平陽（自）［白］燕。

translations.literal: General Huo originally lived at Pingyang in Baiyan.
translations.idiomatic: General Huo Guang originally lived at Pingyang in Baiyan.

sentences.zh: 臣為郎時，與方士考功會旗亭下，為臣言。

translations.literal: When I was a gentleman-attendant, I met the alchemist Kaogong under the Banner Pavilion, and he spoke to me.
translations.idiomatic: When I was a gentleman-attendant, I met the alchemist Kaogong under the Banner Pavilion, and he told me.

sentences.zh: 豈不偉哉！」

translations.literal: Is this not magnificent!"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not magnificent!"
